title: Comparison of normalized common-stage actions at proper compactifications
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with geometric field k, a prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l, a proper k-scheme Y, and a compactification c of a:Y→Spec k [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every normalized compact-support coefficient action S at c and S0 at the identity compactification [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action], their induced functors on the category of literal finite-stage pairs [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] are naturally isomorphic.

source.place: first paragraph: identity compactification and passage through coefficients

proof.text: At each finite coefficient field use the common-refinement integral comparison to the identity compactification, retaining its full coherent quotient system and actual projections. Its scalar square is obtained before total limit from the identity-open restriction square. Both beta maps are the unique tensor-unit mates fixed by the coefficient-action specification, so their adjuncts agree. Faithfulness of coherent reduction identifies the integral maps; no faithfulness of individual evaluations is asserted.
Localize these comparisons and their scalar squares. The coefficient descent argument gives stagewise rational naturality on all tensor morphisms and the common-stage square, including inverse maps.

For an arrow represented over a field L, expand each action as its source beta, finite-stage image of the representative, and inverse target beta. The scalar square moves the comparison past the source beta; rational naturality moves it past the stage map; the inverse scalar square moves it past the target beta. These are equalities over this very L. Extension to larger fields preserves the equality, so it descends to representatives modulo further extension. The inverse components satisfy the same calculation and their composites are identities. Since each action has the specified finite maps and normalized integral beta, this proves the claim for every S and S0, also for zero inputs and identity stages.

theorem properCompactCoefficientActionComparison
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
    (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [IsProper (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    (c : Compactification (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)))
    :
    letI : (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)).Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)) := ⟨𝟙 _⟩
    ∀ S : SfCompactSupportCoefficientAction l D.k (finiteFieldDatumPrimeUnit D l hl) Ω c,
      ∀ S₀ : SfCompactSupportCoefficientAction l D.k (finiteFieldDatumPrimeUnit D l hl) Ω
          (Compactification.ofIsProper (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))),
        Nonempty (S.system.functor ≅ S₀.system.functor)
